summary: This closure review finds the archived, preregistered paired experiment scientifically sound and well documented. The authors fixed most earlier issues: they disclose the unexecuted prespecified comparison and the shared-generation/power mismatch, and they explain the degenerate statistical outcome. One substantive required revision remains: the manuscript still lacks a concise, in-manuscript evidence-to-claim table and a nearest-work comparison matrix and remains provenance-heavy in the main narrative. Resolve these items (from supplied artifacts) and compress provenance into a short appendix or referenced manifest so the paper reads as a normal conference submission rather than an inventory.
critical_issues: No concise evidence-to-claim mapping appears in the manuscript: principal claims are not mapped to specific archived artifacts (paths and SHA256s) within the paper body.
No nearest-work comparison matrix is present in the manuscript that places this run against the closest prior GVR/validator NetOps studies.
Main text remains provenance- and metadata-heavy; this reduces readability and fails to meet normal conference scholarly prose expectations.
required_revisions: Add a compact evidence-to-claim table in the manuscript (1/3–1 page or a concise boxed element) that maps each principal claim (e.g., n11=240, shared-generation semantics, preregistration deviations, degeneracy conclusion) to the specific archived artifact(s) (execution/* or analysis/* paths and SHA-256). Use the supplied archived manifests and hashes; no new experiments or external evidence are required.

Add a nearest-work comparison matrix (approx. 1/2 page) that lists the closest prior studies (title, year, method/architecture, task/data, principal measurable outcome) and, for each, a one-line statement of how the present run differs (preregistration, paired design, shared-generation semantics, synthetic verifier). Populate entries from the verified bibliography already supplied in the artifact bundle.

Compress provenance-heavy material in the main text: move long inventories of artifact paths, long hash lists, and extended provenance bookkeeping into a short 'Artifact appendix' paragraph or a referenced manifest file (e.g., point readers to execution/execution_manifest.json and full hash manifest). Keep only essential artifact citations (preregistration SHA, model_configuration SHA, and where to find the full manifest) in the main five-page paper so that Methods, Results, and Discussion read as conventional scholarly prose. All content can be extracted from the archived artifacts; no new runs are required.
optional_revisions: Include one or two short illustrative examples (1–2 small snippets) from the archived validator traces (e.g., a representative task_manifest entry and its validator_trace) to make construct-validity concerns more tangible.
Add a small table of cluster-stratified acceptance rates (one row per cluster) drawn from execution/task_manifest.jsonl to support the statement that all clusters had 100% acceptance.
Provide a short 'How to reproduce' checklist (3–6 bullets) pointing to the archived files needed for a deterministic rerun (task manifest, RNG seeds, adapter configuration, model configuration).
If space permits, move the full provenance manifest into a single-line URL-like reference to the archived artifact path and include only key SHA256s inline.
